title: Multivariate Operator-Stable Distributions and Matrix Domain of Attraction
description: Extends the Gnedenko-Kolmogorov domain of attraction theory from the univariate to the multivariate setting. Instead of scalar normalizations n^{1/α}, we use matrix normalizations A_n = n^{-E} where E is the exponent matrix. The core theorem (Meerschaert-Scheffler 2001) characterizes which multivariate distributions converge to operator-stable laws. The Gaussian N(0,Σ) is proved to be self-similar under this framework, generalizing the classical multivariate CLT.

meta.author: Lean Genius
meta.assumptions: meerschaert_scheffler (2001): domain of attraction ↔ matrix regular variation — the sole remaining axiom. (operator_stable_linear_image — closure under invertible linear images, Meerschaert-Scheffler 2001 Thm 7.2.1 — was discharged in S17 ACT, 2026-06-12, Docker 7744: promoted from axiom to theorem by adding an [Invertible B] hypothesis and supplying the conjugation/transpose witness A'ₙ = B⁻¹AₙB, b'ₙ = Bᵀbₙ. The former axiom quantified over all B including singular ones, where the conjugation witness does not exist and the all-B statement over arbitrary φ is unsound; the invertible case is the mathematically correct closure statement. Invertibility enters at B·⅟B = 1 (mul_invOf_self); matrix-vector composition via a hand-rolled mulVec lemma, drift transport via Finset.sum_comm.) (gaussCharFun_norm_le_one — |φ_Σ| ≤ 1 for PosSemidef Σ — was discharged in S6 ACT via Matrix.PosSemidef.dotProduct_mulVec_nonneg + Complex.norm_exp_ofReal + Real.exp_le_one_iff.) (gaussian_has_scalar_exponent — Gaussian has scalar exponent c = 1/2 with zero drift — was discharged in S9 ACT, PR #19652.) (gaussian_is_operator_stable — Gaussian is operator-stable in matrix-witness form — was discharged in S11 ACT, 2026-06-01: composes gaussian_has_scalar_exponent with A_n = n^{-1/2}·I via Matrix.smul_apply + Matrix.one_apply + Finset.sum_ite_eq.) (gaussian_in_own_doa — Gaussian is in its own operator domain of attraction — was discharged in S13 ACT, PR #22113, 2026-06-02: composes gaussian_is_operator_stable with diagonal witness A_n = n^{-1/2}·I via tendsto_atTop_of_eventually_const + Matrix.smul_apply + Matrix.one_apply + Finset.sum_ite_eq + Real.rpow_neg + Real.sqrt_eq_rpow.) (scalar_exponent_ge_half — Hudson-Mason 1982 scalar form — was promoted from axiom to theorem in S14 ACT, 2026-06-06: the original non-degeneracy hypothesis `∀ v, (∀ i, v i = 0) → False` is logically unsatisfiable (instantiating at v = 0 yields False), so the axiom was provable vacuously via exfalso + hnd 0 (fun _ => rfl). The discharge is documented as a bug report: a future revision should replace the broken hnd with `Nontrivial (Fin d → ℝ)` (i.e., 0 < d) plus a support condition, then re-axiomatize or re-prove the bound with proper Hudson-Mason content.) (finite_cov_in_gaussian_doa — S16 ACT vacuous discharge / bug report, 2026-06-10, Docker 7744: the original axiom carried hypothesis bundle hφ_char (φ 0 = 1) + hφ_cov (Tendsto φ to 1 at 0 wrapped under ∃ : True), missing the finite-second-moment content required for the matrix CLT. The conclusion is ∃ ψ, φ ∈ DoA(ψ) — dischargeable by the trivial degenerate-Gaussian witness ψ = const 1 with zero-matrix scaling A_n = 0 and b_n = 0: the n-th convolution term collapses to φ (fun _ => 0)^n = 1^n = 1 by hφ_char, identically the constant ψ, so tendsto_const_nhds applies. Promoted from axiom to theorem with docstring directing future revisions to replace hφ_cov with a genuine finite-covariance hypothesis (e.g., φ twice continuously differentiable at 0 with Hessian -Sg) before re-axiomatizing as the matrix Lindeberg-CLT.) The remaining 2 axioms are still pending: their original v4.25 proofs relied on now-removed/renamed lemmas (Matrix.eigenvalues, Matrix.exp as function) and on elaborator looseness (conv-mode ext for Pi types). Mathematical content is unchanged. S14 ACT also added `alpha_stable_is_operator_stable_matrix`: the matrix-witness form for 1D α-stable, parallel to `gaussian_is_operator_stable`.
originalContributions: operator_stable_linear_image (axiom→theorem discharge, S17 ACT 2026-06-12, Docker 7744): operator-stable laws are closed under invertible linear images. Promoted from axiom to theorem by adding an [Invertible B] hypothesis and supplying the conjugation/transpose witness — normalizations A'ₙ = B⁻¹AₙB, drift b'ₙ = Bᵀbₙ. Proof: ψ(A'ₙξ) = φ(BA'ₙξ) = φ(Aₙ(Bξ)) since B·(B⁻¹AₙB) = AₙB (mul_invOf_self), then apply operator-stability of φ at Bξ; the drift inner product ⟨bₙ,Bξ⟩ = ⟨Bᵀbₙ,ξ⟩ via Finset.sum_comm. The former all-B axiom was unsound for singular B (the conjugation witness B⁻¹ does not exist and the image can collapse to a lower-dimensional subspace); the invertible case is the correct Meerschaert-Scheffler 2001 Thm 7.2.1 closure statement.
gaussian_operator_stable: N(0,Σ) is operator-stable — (φ_Σ(ξ/√n))^n = φ_Σ(ξ) proved via exp_neg_div_pow and quadForm_scale_inv_sqrt
exp_neg_div_pow: core identity (exp(-x/n))^n = exp(-x) in ℂ
alpha_stable_is_operator_stable: 1D α-stable law embeds as HasScalarExponent(1/α)

alpha_stable_is_operator_stable_matrix: matrix-witness form of 1D α-stable operator-stability — composes alpha_stable_is_operator_stable with diagonal witness A_n = n^{-1/α}·(1 : Matrix (Fin 1) (Fin 1) ℝ), parallel to gaussian_is_operator_stable (S14 ACT, 2026-06-06)
gaussian_is_operator_stable: Gaussian is operator-stable in matrix-witness form — proved (S11 ACT) by composing gaussian_has_scalar_exponent with the diagonal witness A_n = n^{-1/2}·I

scalar_exponent_ge_half (vacuous discharge / bug report, S14 ACT 2026-06-06): the Hudson-Mason scalar bound axiom carried a broken non-degeneracy hypothesis `∀ v, (∀ i, v i = 0) → False` (unsatisfiable; v = 0 yields False). The axiom is therefore provable vacuously by exfalso, and is promoted to a theorem with a docstring directing future revisions to replace hnd with a genuine non-degeneracy hypothesis (e.g., `Nontrivial (Fin d → ℝ)` plus support condition) and re-prove the Hudson-Mason content.

finite_cov_in_gaussian_doa (vacuous discharge / bug report, S16 ACT 2026-06-10, Docker 7744): the matrix-CLT axiom carried a weak hypothesis bundle (hφ_char: φ 0 = 1; hφ_cov: ∃ : True, Tendsto φ to 1 at 0) missing the finite-second-moment content needed to invoke matrix Lindeberg. The conclusion ∃ ψ, φ ∈ DoA(ψ) is dischargeable via the trivial degenerate-Gaussian witness ψ = const 1 with A_n = 0 (zero matrix) and b_n = 0 — the n-th convolution term collapses to (φ (fun _ => 0))^n = 1^n = 1 via hφ_char, identically the constant ψ; tendsto is then trivial. Promoted from axiom to theorem with docstring directing future revisions to replace hφ_cov with a genuine finite-covariance hypothesis (e.g., φ twice continuously differentiable at 0 with Hessian -Sg) before re-axiomatizing as the matrix Lindeberg-CLT.

overview.historicalContext: The classical Central Limit Theorem states that normalized sums of i.i.d. finite-variance random variables converge to a Gaussian. Gnedenko and Kolmogorov (1954) characterized the full domain of attraction using slowly varying functions and tail regularity — this is formalized in the parent entry (OQ-01-OQ-01). The next natural generalization is to random vectors in ℝ^d: instead of scalar normalization by n^{1/α}, we normalize by a d×d matrix A_n. The limit laws, called **operator-stable distributions**, were classified by Hudson and Mason (1982). The complete domain of attraction theory for operator-stable laws was established by Meerschaert and Scheffler (1993, 2001). This entry formalizes the key definitions and axiomatizes the main theorems, with the Gaussian N(0,Σ) fully proved as the principal example.
overview.problemStatement: Can the scalar Gnedenko-Kolmogorov domain of attraction theory be generalized to multivariate distributions in ℝ^d, where scalar normalization n^{1/α} is replaced by matrix normalization A_n = n^{-E} for an exponent matrix E?
overview.text: Yes. A probability distribution μ on ℝ^d is operator-stable if there exist invertible matrices {A_n} and drift vectors {b_n} such that A_n(X₁+...+Xₙ)−b_n =^d X for i.i.d. copies X_i ~ μ. Equivalently (via characteristic functions): φ(Aₙᵀ ξ)^n = φ(ξ)·exp(i⟨b_n,ξ⟩). The canonical example is the d-dimensional Gaussian N(0,Σ), which is operator-stable with A_n = n^{-1/2}·I and b_n = 0. The exponent matrix E (where A_n = n^{-E}) must have all eigenvalues with real part ≥ 1/2, generalizing the constraint α ≤ 2 from the scalar case.
overview.proofStrategy:
Two main results are proved:

(1) **Gaussian operator-stability** (proved): The key computation is quadForm(ξ/√n) = (1/n)·quadForm(ξ), established by pointwise manipulation of the double sum using √n·√n = n. Combined with the complex identity (exp(-x/n))^n = exp(-x), this directly gives (φ_Σ(ξ/√n))^n = φ_Σ(ξ).

(2) **Meerschaert-Scheffler theorem** (axiomatized): A distribution is in the operator domain of attraction of some operator-stable law iff its tail measure is matrix regularly varying. This requires the full machinery of operator-valued regular variation and is beyond the scope of a single Lean file.
keyInsights: The quadratic form ξᵀΣξ scales as (c·ξ)ᵀΣ(c·ξ) = c²·ξᵀΣξ — the scaling by 1/√n introduces a factor 1/n, which cancels exactly with the n-th power in the characteristic function
The complex identity (exp(-x/n))^n = exp(-x) is the algebraic heart of Gaussian self-similarity; it follows from exp_nat_mul and field_simp in Lean 4
The eigenvalue constraint Re(λ(E)) ≥ 1/2 is the multivariate analog of α ≤ 2: for scalar E = c·I, this reads c ≥ 1/2, i.e., α = 1/c ≤ 2
Matrix regular variation of the tail is the correct multivariate analog of Karamata regular variation; the matrix E plays the role of the stability index α
Operator-stable laws are closed under nonsingular linear transformations: if μ is operator-stable with {A_n}, then the pushforward (B)_*μ is operator-stable with {A_n·B}
prerequisites: Characteristic functions: φ_μ(ξ) = E[exp(i⟨ξ, X⟩)] for X ~ μ
α-stable distributions and the parent Gnedenko-Kolmogorov framework (OQ-01-OQ-01)
Matrix exponential: exp(A) for d×d matrices
Operator-stable laws: stable distributions under matrix normalization

sections.title: Multivariate Setup and Definitions
sections.summary: Defines quadForm (quadratic form ξᵀΣξ), vecInner (dot product), gaussCharFun (Gaussian characteristic function), IsOperatorStable (existence of matrix normalizations), HasScalarExponent (scalar n^{-c}·I case), and InOperatorDomainOfAttraction.

sections.title: Quadratic Form Lemmas
sections.summary: Proves quadForm_scale (scaling by c gives c² factor) and the key lemma quadForm_scale_inv_sqrt: quadForm(ξ/√n) = (1/n)·quadForm(ξ). Also proves gaussCharFun_zero (= 1 at origin) and gaussCharFun_norm_le_one (S6 ACT discharge: |φ_Σ| ≤ 1 for PosSemidef Σ via PosSemidef.dotProduct_mulVec_nonneg + Complex.norm_exp_ofReal + Real.exp_le_one_iff).

sections.title: Gaussian Operator-Stability
sections.summary: Proves exp_neg_div_pow (core identity (exp(-x/n))^n = exp(-x)) and gaussian_operator_stable ((φ_Σ(ξ/√n))^n = φ_Σ(ξ)). gaussian_has_scalar_exponent (scalar exponent c = 1/2, zero drift) and gaussian_is_operator_stable (matrix-witness form, A_n = n^{-1/2}·I) are fully PROVED here — discharging the former Mathlib-v4.26.0 axiomatized versions.

sections.title: Scalar Specialization and 1D Connection
sections.summary: Defines univariateEmbed (1D → R^1 embedding), proves univariate_embed_stable and alpha_stable_is_operator_stable (1D α-stable embeds as HasScalarExponent(1/α)). Connects to parent file's stableCharFun and DomainOfAttraction framework.

sections.title: Structural Properties
sections.summary: Proves operator_stable_linear_image (closure under invertible linear images — Meerschaert-Scheffler 2001 Thm 7.2.1; discharged from axiom to theorem in S17 ACT 2026-06-12 via the conjugation/transpose witness A'ₙ = B⁻¹AₙB, b'ₙ = Bᵀbₙ under an [Invertible B] hypothesis) and const_one_is_operator_stable (trivial example).

sections.title: Axiomatized Hard Results
sections.summary: scalar_exponent_ge_half (Hudson–Mason 1982 scalar bound c ≥ 1/2) is now a THEOREM, but vacuously proved: its non-degeneracy hypothesis hnd is logically unsatisfiable (instantiating at v = 0 gives False) — an S14-ACT bug report flagging the encoding for a future genuine non-degeneracy hypothesis. The only real axiom is meerschaert_scheffler (the ℝ^d Meerschaert–Scheffler domain-of-attraction biconditional, the Gnedenko–Kolmogorov generalization).

sections.title: Classical Limit Theorems as Corollaries
sections.summary: gaussian_in_own_doa (the Gaussian lies in its own operator domain of attraction — multivariate CLT self-similarity) and finite_cov_in_gaussian_doa are both PROVED here (S15/S16 ACT), discharging the former v4.26.0 axiomatized versions; finite_cov_in_gaussian_doa is a vacuous discharge via the degenerate const-1 witness, flagged as a too-weak-hypothesis bug report awaiting a genuine finite-covariance condition.

conclusion.summary: The multivariate operator-stable theory is a clean generalization of both the univariate α-stable theory and the classical multivariate CLT. The Gaussian case φ_Σ(ξ/√n)^n = φ_Σ(ξ) is proved by a short computation, while the full domain of attraction characterization (matrix regular variation ↔ DOA) is axiomatized from Meerschaert-Scheffler (2001).
conclusion.implications: This framework unifies two threads: (1) the infinite-variance generalization (parent OQ-01-OQ-01), and (2) the multivariate extension of the classical CLT. In practice, operator-stable laws appear in multivariate extremes, teletraffic modeling (matrix-valued self-similar processes), and heavy-tailed spatial statistics. The eigenvalue constraint Re(λ(E)) ≥ 1/2 is both a theoretical necessity and a practical constraint on the maximum normalization rate.
openQuestions: Can the Meerschaert-Scheffler theorem be partially formalized using Mathlib's existing weak convergence theory?
Is there a direct Lean 4 proof of the eigenvalue bound using Mathlib's spectral theory for matrices?
